One Nation faced scrutiny on two fronts, with the Sydney Morning Herald reporting on its leader's taxpayer-funded expenses in a former trade role and the Guardian reporting on a NSW candidate who manufactures firearms and opposes the post-Bondi gun laws. Locally, the Illawarra Mercury reports hospital access pressures at an "unprecedented" level and a new South Coast Line timetable that lengthens airport journeys from mid-November.

briefing.topLine: Labor used the pre-election period to promise a further $11 billion cut to gross debt over the next decade without privatisation, a plan the AFR reports would draw on energy dividends to reduce borrowing costs. One Nation faced scrutiny on two fronts, with the Sydney Morning Herald reporting on its leader's taxpayer-funded expenses in a former trade role and the Guardian reporting on a NSW candidate who manufactures firearms and opposes the post-Bondi gun laws. Locally, the Illawarra Mercury reports hospital access pressures at an "unprecedented" level and a new South Coast Line timetable that lengthens airport journeys from mid-November.
briefing.localWatch: Two service questions dominate the region: the Illawarra Mercury reports more than 130 people stranded in the local hospital system, and a South Coast Line timetable change from 15 November that it says adds 15 to 30 minutes to Sydney Airport trips. Kiama Council has welcomed the shelving of proposed funding changes and set out a new four-pillar advocacy plan, while Shoalhaven's tourist paid-parking proposal has drawn community pushback.

stories.headline: Illawarra hospital crisis hits 'unprecedented' level with more than 130 people stranded
stories.summary: The Illawarra Mercury reports that pressure on the region's hospitals has reached what it describes as an unprecedented level, with more than 130 people stranded in the system.

stories.headline: Travel to airport will take how much longer? Reality of new train timetable revealed
stories.summary: A new South Coast Line timetable starting 15 November will add between 15 and 30 minutes to trips to Sydney Airport, according to the Illawarra Mercury, which reports residents have voiced frustration at the changes.

stories.headline: Council welcomes decision to call off proposed funding changes
stories.summary: Kiama Council has published a statement welcoming a decision to abandon proposed funding changes. No further detail was supplied beyond the council's announcement.

stories.headline: Mayor’s update: The four pillars of Kiama’s new advocacy plan
stories.summary: In a mayoral update, Kiama Council sets out four pillars underpinning its new advocacy plan. The supplied text does not detail what each pillar covers.

stories.headline: ‘Load of sh-t’: Community slams tourist paid parking push
stories.summary: The Daily Telegraph reports that a proposal for tourist paid parking in the Shoalhaven has been criticised by local residents.

stories.headline: Where will it land? Battle brewing over return of Nowra's iconic landmark
stories.summary: Plans to install a replacement Seahawk replica in Nowra have stalled, the South Coast Register reports, with MP Fiona Phillips and Shoalhaven City Council at odds over where it should go.

stories.headline: Labor’s plan to cut $11 billion of debt without privatisation
stories.summary: The NSW Government says a re-elected Minns Labor Government would cut gross debt by a further $11 billion over the next decade while keeping NSW what it calls Australia's most fiscally responsible state, and without privatisation. The Australian Financial Review reports the plan would use energy dividends to reduce borrowing costs.

stories.headline: Firearms manufacturer standing for One Nation in NSW opposes post-Bondi gun laws that ban his rifles
stories.summary: The Guardian reports that Jeff Bacon, managing director of Oceania Precision and a One Nation candidate in NSW, opposes the post-Bondi firearms laws that ban rifles he makes. The paper reports the NSW party leader has described him as the party's go-to person on the firearms industry.

stories.headline: Revealed: One Nation leader’s seven-month Sydney hotel stay that cost taxpayers $20,000
stories.summary: The Sydney Morning Herald reports that One Nation leader Mike Newman accrued $211,000 in taxpayer-funded flights, five-star hotels and restaurant and bar costs across 28 months while serving as a senior trade commissioner to Japan, including a seven-month Sydney hotel stay the paper puts at about $20,000.

stories.headline: Students see red: protest breaks out at Pauline Hanson's Toronto fundraiser
stories.summary: The Newcastle Herald reports that young activists protested outside a One Nation fundraiser in the Hunter attended by Pauline Hanson, objecting to what they called the party's "racist, denialist" ideology and calling for venues to refuse bookings.

stories.headline: Reforms pass Parliament, paving the way for a stronger firefighting fleet
stories.summary: The NSW Government says legislation modernising the management of more than 6,000 Rural Fire Service firefighting and support vehicles has passed Parliament, which it says will make the fleet more reliable.

stories.headline: $2m payday for home battery owners as heatwave catches grid off guard
stories.summary: The ABC reports that unseasonal heat, coal outages and transmission constraints pushed NSW power prices sharply higher this week, and that home battery owners earned about $2 million as a result.

stories.headline: 'Crying in the dark': bereaved begging for reform
stories.summary: Families of people who are missing and presumed dead have given evidence to a public inquiry about what they allege were failures by police investigators, the South Coast Register reports. The allegations have not been tested.

stories.headline: Wentworth Park’s next chapter: more sporting fields and open space for the community
stories.summary: The NSW Government says it is proceeding with plans to convert the former greyhound racing site at Wentworth Park into community sporting fields and public open space within an expanded 14-hectare parkland.

stories.headline: Liberal Party settles class action over nominations fiasco
stories.summary: The Australian reports that the NSW Liberal Party has agreed to settle a class action arising from the council election nominations failure.

stories.headline: Council suspended after GM sacked in wake of mayoral vote hat-draw blunder
stories.summary: The ABC reports that a northern NSW council has been suspended for three months following a tied mayoral vote decided by a draw from a hat in which the wrong candidate was declared mayor, and the subsequent sacking of its general manager.

stories.headline: Brethren member says he encouraged Liberal campaigning
stories.summary: The son of the Plymouth Brethren's global leader has told an inquiry into election campaigning that he encouraged others to picket for the Liberal Party, the South Coast Register reports. A second report says the probe has been likened to the Spanish Inquisition.

stories.headline: Councillor told woman it was a 'pity' she wasn't bashed, investigator finds
stories.summary: An investigator has found that a Kempsey Shire councillor told a woman it was a "pity" she had not been assaulted by an alleged domestic violence offender, the ABC reports. The ABC reports the councillor maintains his social media account was hacked, and that there are calls for him to resign.

stories.headline: Chase on in states’ ‘debt race to the bottom’
stories.summary: The Australian argues the states are chasing Victoria in what it calls a debt race to the bottom, a framing that lands the same day NSW Labor announced its own debt reduction pledge. Only the headline was supplied.

elsewhere.text: Ben Raue has updated his Victorian state election candidate lists and asks whether the field will be bigger than 2022 — a useful benchmark for tracking NSW nominations in 2027.
